etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English glisnen, glistnen, from Old English glisnian, itself from Proto-West Germanic *glisnōn, while ultimately deriving from Proto-Germanic *glisnōną.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, of a wet or greasy surface) To reflect light with a glittering luster; to sparkle, coruscate, glint or flash.

quote.citation: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I, page 202:
quote.text: The sun was fierce, the land seemed to glisten and drip with steam.

definitions.definition: A glistening shine from a wet surface.

quote.citation: 1920, D.H. Lawrence, chapter 1, in Women in Love:
quote.text: In his clear northern flesh and his fair hair was a glisten like sunshine refracted through crystals of ice.
